# onpager_work_calendar_entry (Resource)

Manage one work calendar entry with its own UUID and revision.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Local clocks use the provider request timezone; source weekdays stay UTC.
resource "onpager_work_calendar_entry" "example" {
  team_id     = var.team_id
  calendar_id = var.calendar_id
  name        = "Maintenance"
  effect      = "non_working"
  rule_type   = "weekly"
  weekdays    = ["MO", "WE"]
  start_date  = "2027-01-01"
  end_date    = "2027-12-31"
  clock = {
    reference_date = "2024-01-01"
    windows = [
      { starts_at = "2024-01-01T09:00:00", ends_at = "2024-01-01T10:00:01" },
      { starts_at = "2024-01-03T09:00:00", ends_at = "2024-01-03T10:00:01" },
    ]
  }
}

variable "team_id" {
  description = "Existing owning team UUID."
  type        = string
}

variable "calendar_id" {
  description = "Existing work-calendar UUID in this team."
  type        = string
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `calendar_id` (String) Owning calendar UUID. Changing it replaces this resource. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `effect` (String) Calendar effect: `working` or `non_working`.
- `name` (String) Exception name; it does not identify the entry. Must be nonempty without leading or trailing whitespace.
- `rule_type` (String) Exception rule: `date` requires start_date; `date_range` requires start_date and end_date; `datetime_interval` requires starts_at and ends_at; `weekly` requires weekdays; `yearly` requires month and day. Only weekly/yearly accept optional date bounds and clock.
- `team_id` (String) Owning team UUID. Changing it replaces this resource. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `clock` (Attributes) Dated recurring clock accepted only for weekly/yearly. Omission or null means the entire source UTC day. Source weekdays/month/day retain UTC identities. The backend must resolve all windows to one uniform whole-second UTC clock and duration fitting the source day; DST errors remain backend diagnostics. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--clock))
- `day` (Number) Source UTC day of month, required only for `yearly`. Must form a valid date with `month`, including February 29; zero is invalid.
- `end_date` (String) Inclusive source UTC date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Required for `date_range`; optional upper bound for `weekly` and `yearly`. Must not precede `start_date`; empty strings are invalid.
- `ends_at` (String) Exclusive end instant, required only for `datetime_interval`. Use local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` or RFC3339 with an explicit offset, at most six fractional digits (microsecond precision). Local values use the provider request timezone; the backend resolves them and rejects DST gaps or ambiguity. Must follow `starts_at`; empty strings are invalid. Equivalent instants retain configured state. Changing an explicit provider timezone plans an update for local inputs.
- `month` (Number) Source UTC month from 1 through 12. Required only for `yearly`; zero is invalid. Must form a valid date with `day`.
- `start_date` (String) Source UTC date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Required for `date` and `date_range`; optional inclusive lower bound for `weekly` and `yearly`. Empty strings are invalid.
- `starts_at` (String) Start instant, required only for `datetime_interval`. Use local `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` or RFC3339 with an explicit offset, at most six fractional digits (microsecond precision). Local values use the provider request timezone; the backend resolves them and rejects DST gaps or ambiguity. Must precede `ends_at`; empty strings are invalid. Equivalent instants retain configured state. Changing an explicit provider timezone plans an update for local inputs.
- `weekdays` (Set of String) Nonempty set of source UTC weekdays: `MO`, `TU`, `WE`, `TH`, `FR`, `SA`, `SU`. Required only for `weekly`; an empty set is invalid.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `request_timezone` (String) Explicit provider request timezone last applied to local datetime inputs. Null when the provider timezone is omitted or all inputs have explicit offsets. Changing the explicit provider timezone plans an update for local inputs; refresh alone preserves saved instants. The backend interprets local clocks and reports DST ambiguity or nonexistent times.
- `revision` (Number) Entry revision used in strong numeric `If-Match` for replacing or deleting this exception. Independent of parent settings and sibling entries; stale revisions report a conflict.

### Nested Schema for `clock`

Required:

- `reference_date` (String) Explicit fixed UTC source date: 2024-01-01 for weekly, or the selected yearly month/day in leap year 2024.
- `windows` (Attributes Set) One through seven whole-second dated windows, covering the selected source days. Local datetimes and explicit RFC3339 offsets are sent unchanged. The displayed local date may differ from its source UTC weekday/date. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--clock--windows))

<a id="nestedatt--clock--windows"></a>
### Nested Schema for `clock.windows`

Required:

- `ends_at` (String) Exclusive end; same formats as starts_at and must follow it. Mixed local and explicit-offset ordering is checked by the backend.
- `starts_at` (String) Inclusive local datetime in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss form or explicit RFC3339 instant. Sent unchanged; the backend resolves local input in the provider request timezone and rejects DST ambiguity or gaps.

## Import

Import using `team_uuid/calendar_uuid/entry_uuid`. Import reads the exact scoped
entry and adopts explicit-offset API timestamps.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_work_calendar_entry.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666/77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_work_calendar_entry.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111/66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666/77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777
```

## Lifecycle

Supply only fields applicable to the selected `rule_type`; omit other fields or
set them to null. Explicit empty and zero values still count as supplied and are
rejected when they belong to another rule type.

Each entry has its own UUID and numeric revision. Creation requires no parent
revision; updates replace the entry using its own revision. Sibling entries,
calendar settings and schedules are managed separately. Conflicts retain state
and require a new plan.

Destroy deletes the entry, including authorized cleanup under an inactive team.
Archiving the parent calendar retains its other entries. Confirmed `404
not_found` removes state; authorization, transport and conflict errors retain
it.

## Dates, recurring clocks and timezone

Date-only values identify UTC source dates. Date ranges and recurring date
bounds are inclusive; timestamp intervals have an exclusive end.

Recurring `clock` objects declare `reference_date` and a `windows` set. Weekly
clocks use fixed UTC source Monday `2024-01-01`; yearly clocks use the selected
month and day in leap year 2024, including `2024-02-29`. Supply one to seven
whole-second windows covering the selected source days. The API must resolve
them to a uniform UTC clock and duration that fits each source UTC day. Local
display dates can differ from the selected UTC weekday or yearly date. An
omitted or null clock means the full UTC day. Reads use this fixed projection.

Datetime interval endpoints and recurring clock windows accept local
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss` values or explicit-offset RFC3339 instants. Datetime
intervals allow up to six fractional digits; recurring clocks use whole seconds.
Input is sent unchanged. The API resolves local values in the provider request
timezone, stores UTC, returns offset timestamps and rejects DST ambiguity or
gaps. Explicit offsets identify absolute instants.

State preserves configured strings and precision while authoritative server
instants remain equivalent. Private timestamp bindings detect real drift across
request-zone changes; configured strings and bindings persist in Terraform
state. Import adopts explicit-offset API values. Changing an explicit provider
`timezone` plans an update through computed `request_timezone` for local inputs;
apply reinterprets those strings in the new zone. Refresh preserves stored
instants. Omitted provider timezone follows the API actor's default without
explicit zone tracking.

## Permissions

Requires owning-team grants `team_work_calendars.read` and
`team_work_calendars.update`, including entry creation and deletion. Service
accounts are supported.
